trigger: Wave 6. Two units and the orchestrator all certified the crash-class survivors at validate_run.py:6698/:6705 as 'pre-existing, not a regression' on the strength of a HEAD control - 'it crashes on HEAD too'. U28's panel lens 2 falsified it and the orchestrator confirmed by measurement: the census of the last PRE-RUN commit f547aef is 190, the shipped tree is 192, and the delta is exactly those two survivors, introduced by THIS run's own commit 4fb475d. The HEAD control was true and worthless. validate_run.py is byte-identical to HEAD (sha256 verified), so the control compared a file WITH ITSELF and returned 2 == 2 by construction. The claim survived three separate recordings - RESUME.md, PROGRESS.md and U28's brief - because each inherited it rather than re-deriving it.
lesson: A regression control must be taken against the last commit BEFORE the run began, never against HEAD. The moment a run commits any of its own work, HEAD CONTAINS THAT WORK, and 'it is also broken at HEAD' stops distinguishing pre-existing from self-inflicted - it degenerates into comparing the working tree with itself. The failure is invisible precisely when the run is being diligent: a run that commits early and often destroys its own baseline the earliest. The general form is that a control is only a control if the two sides CAN differ; a comparison whose sides are byte-identical proves the identity, not the property. Here the cost was the sharpest possible: a run whose entire subject is a predicate policing a crash class shipped two fresh instances of that very class and certified them as somebody else's. And the mis-classification is not confined to one artifact type: the same commit produced both a crash-class regression and locator drift, and BOTH were booked as pre-existing. When a run edits a file that other artifacts cite BY LINE NUMBER, it manufactures drift by construction - so 'pre-existing' must be re-derived per artifact class against the base commit, never inferred once and reused.
how_to_apply: Record the run's BASE COMMIT at bootstrap and control against that ref for every regression claim - `git show <base>:<path>` into a temp file, never `git show HEAD:<path>` once the run has committed. Before publishing any control, assert the two sides are NOT identical (a sha256 or a diff-stat), and treat an empty diff as an INVALID control rather than a passing one - the same fail-loud arm the run's own instruments use when they parse zero items. When a control's result equals the measured value exactly, ask whether it could have returned anything else. And treat an inherited provenance claim as unmeasured: 'pre-existing' asserted in a brief, a handoff, or a prior debrief is a claim to re-derive, not a fact to carry.
